findings.message: moveProposal reads the proposal without a row lock and then updates it unconditionally by id. Every other writer that changes a release's proposal rows locks them first (lockProposals, rounds 18 to 20). Because of that, a board/MCP/chat Move can overwrite the 'released' phase that a concurrent Prod deployment just set. The move's UPDATE waits on the deployment's lock, then re-checks only `id = ...` and goes ahead. Fix: read with `for update` (or use lockProposals) before the phase check, or make the update conditional (`where id = ... and phase <> 'released'`) and refuse when no row changed. Add a two-worker race test (move held vs. Prod deploy, both orders) that fails without the lock.
findings.scenario: CON-010 is verified in v2.4.0. moveProposal(CON-010 -> building) reads phase 'verified'. Meanwhile recordDeployment(v2.4.0, Prod) commits and sets it to released. The move's update then runs: CON-010 ends up phase 'building' with released_at set on a release that is live in Prod. The outbox has 'released' followed by a stale 'verified -> building' event.

findings.message: There are two rules for whether a release is live in Prod, and they disagree. nextStep/listReleases look at the latest non-voided record per environment (`status === 'deployed'` on Prod). assignProposals and voidDeployment look at any non-voided deployment with `released = true`. A later Prod record with status 'testing' or 'rolled-back' makes the map say the release isn't live, while the proposals stay Released and the service refuses new proposals as 'already live in Prod'. Use one definition, ideally the `released` flag, for both the map and the services.
findings.scenario: Record v1 -> Prod deployed (proposals released). Then record v1 -> Prod status rolled-back. The Releases page shows 'Retry Prod' (not Live), but the proposals still show 'In Prod', and setReleaseProposals(v1, [new key]) fails with 'already live in Prod'.

findings.message: Round 17 made a duplicate version in createRelease fail with a clear error, but two other duplicate-key paths still surface a raw Postgres unique violation: tagRelease renaming to a version the project already has, and createProject with an existing key. Use the same pattern on both (check, or `on conflict do nothing` and throw a clear error) and add variant tests.
findings.scenario: tagRelease(CON, v2.5.0 -> v2.4.0) throws 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "release_project_id_version_key"' instead of 'CON already has a release v2.4.0'. The same happens for create_project with key CON.

findings.message: releaseEditAction runs tagRelease and setReleaseProposals as two separate service transactions. If the second fails, the re-tag is already committed and the redirect never runs. The user stays on a page whose URL names a version that no longer exists, and the only error they see is about the proposals. Validate the proposals first, or do the re-tag and the proposal change in one service/transaction.
findings.scenario: On v2.5.0, change the tag to v2.6.0 and tick a proposal that already shipped in another release. setReleaseProposals throws 'already shipped', but the release is now v2.6.0. Reloading /delivery/releases/CON/v2.5.0 shows 'Release not found'.

findings.message: The contract read functions (listProjectRefs, getProjectRef, managedProjectIds) take only a tenant tx and apply no caller data scope or permission check. architecture.md says cross-module reads go through contract functions 'which apply the caller's data scope', and the file header claims they do. Take the caller's viewer/context and filter by delivery:read and its scope, or fix the header and doc claim.
findings.scenario: A time-module screen for an Engineer whose grant is @assigned calls listProjectRefs(tx) and gets every active project in the tenant, including manager_user_id.

findings.message: A malformed JSON body (here and in /oauth/register) throws a SyntaxError that oauthError maps to 500 server_error. Malformed client input should be a 400 invalid_request. Catch the parse failure and raise OAuthError('invalid_request').
findings.scenario: POST /oauth/register with body '{bad' and content-type application/json returns 500 server_error, not 400 invalid_request.

findings.message: When no data region is set and AI isn't blocked, the Data region ticket says 'Database, files and AI in region' even though no region is defined or checked. Show something like 'No region policy' instead.
findings.scenario: Default policy with ZDR confirmed: the ticket shows 'Not set' with the note 'Database, files and AI in region'.

findings.message: Because of `continue-on-error: true`, plus the gate that skips silently when secrets are missing, a sync that failed or never ran shows as a green check. Add a visible warning or annotation (::warning::) for both the skipped and the failed cases.
findings.scenario: An expired AMAX_SYNC_TOKEN makes the import throw, and the workflow run still shows as successful.

findings.message: The README's Events and Contracts lines leave out delivery.proposal.rekeyed and the ProposalRekeyed payload type, which contracts.ts and module.ts emit and export.

Adding an environment whose name matches an existing one apart from case quietly turns into an update of that row (envByName is case-insensitive) and reports success. The 'Add environment' form should refuse with 'already has an environment called X'.
findings.scenario: With 'Staging' present, submitting 'Add environment' with 'staging' succeeds silently and nothing is added.

findings.message: The round-18/19 rule says every writer that changes a release's proposal rows locks them first. moveProposal breaks that rule. It reads the proposal with a plain select and then updates it by id with no lock and no phase guard. A board or MCP move that runs alongside a Prod recordDeployment is applied after the deploy commits and overwrites 'released'. Fix: lock the row the same way the other writers do (`lockProposals(tx, sql\`id = ${p.id}\`)`, or `select ... for update`) before reading the phase. Alternatively add `and phase = ${p.phase}` to the update and refuse when no row changes. Add a two-session race test against recordDeployment that uses holdAfterReleaseLock.
findings.scenario: CON-012 is verified and in v2.4.0. The move to 'building' reads phase=verified. The Prod recordDeployment of v2.4.0 then locks the row, sets it to released and commits. The move's update runs next. Result: CON-012 is phase 'building' with released_at set, inside a release that is live in Prod. The outbox holds a 'released' event followed by a stale 'verified→building' event.

findings.message: Round 17 made createRelease refuse a duplicate version with a clear message. tagRelease, the second path that sets a version, still fails with a raw unique-constraint error on (project_id, version). It also has a 40-character limit on the new version that createRelease does not have. Check for the conflict and refuse clearly, and use the same version schema in both services.
findings.scenario: tagRelease CON v2.5.0 → v2.4.0 → raw Postgres 23505 error instead of 'CON already has a release v2.4.0'.

findings.message: Engineer is granted `delivery:proposal:create@assigned` and `delivery:proposal:move@assigned`, but no installed resolver fills `assignedProjects`. delivery's viewerScopes returns only managedProjects. These grants therefore never take effect for a real user, while the tool list (canEver) still offers create_proposal and move_proposal to Engineers. Either document that they depend on allocations, or leave them out until a resolver provides assigned projects.
findings.scenario: An Engineer assigned to FLT calls move_proposal FLT-015 → ScopeError 'outside your data scope'.
